  1. Show HN: Mastra Factory, the open-source software factory we use to build Mastra

    • AI
    • Open Source
    • Software Development

    145 points · 42 comments · 18 Nov 2026, 16:53 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Mastra Factory is an open-source, configurable agentic kanban system for software work, operated through a web UI and Slack. Its self-post says Mastra uses durable agents, memory, a cited Markdown wiki, PR-comment signals, cloud sandboxes, and a coding harness; it reports 238 Factory-opened-and-merged PRs and 630 human PRs in one week, alongside hosted and self-hosted options.

    Discussion — Discussion centered on the maintainers' decision to close their main repository to outside contributors because of low-value automated PRs, while requesting high-quality issue reproductions. Readers asked how autonomy, plans, model/harness integration, agent identity, UX validation, and human approval work. The team said lower-risk work can be more automated and that sandbox preview environments support UI testing.

  2. Show HN: Alloy CSS, dialogs, menus and tabs that work with JavaScript off

    • Design
    • Software Development

    210 points · 38 comments · 17 Nov 2026, 15:07 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Alloy CSS is a fixed-scale CSS kit for server-rendered interfaces that uses current browser features such as dialog, popover, commandfor, and :has(). Its linked invoice-dashboard example is one HTML file with no JavaScript while retaining menus, dialog, drawer, tabs, tooltips, toast, and other interactions.

    Discussion — Supporters welcomed progressive enhancement and less client-side JavaScript. Skeptics raised accessibility, CSS-name conflicts, and complexity concerns; the author said Alloy is a new design system rather than a drop-in utility layer. Discussion also debated which browser capabilities should become native and where JavaScript remains necessary.

    Week of 2026-11-20

  3. Ask HN: If AI tools are so good, why isn't your bug backlog empty?

    • AI
    • Software Development

    103 points · 117 comments · 16 Nov 2026, 17:20 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — The Ask HN post asked why bug backlogs are not empty if AI coding tools are as capable as advertised, inviting concrete experience rather than a claim about a particular product.

    Discussion — Respondents described AI as helpful for triage, fixes, tests, and refactors but limited by unclear requirements, integration work, validation, and organizational prioritization. Some reported substantial backlog reduction; others said the tools create or reveal additional work.

  4. Show HN: Coral – Open-source gateway where agents write their own tools

    • AI
    • Security
    • Software Development

    52 points · 24 comments · 16 Nov 2026, 14:14 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Coral is an open-source, self-hosted gateway for agents that lets them write reusable TypeScript custom tools while enforcing policies and managed identities. The HN post says programs run in V8 isolates without direct network access or credentials.

    Discussion — Discussion examined code-mode agents, custom-tool reuse, policy boundaries, security, and claimed task speed and cost reductions. Readers asked how the system compares with MCP-style integrations and how it avoids unsafe permissions.

  5. Show HN: Unref – A Python dead code finder built on Ruff's parser

    • Python
    • Software Development

    63 points · 18 comments · 16 Nov 2026, 13:30 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Unref is a Rust-based Python dead-code finder built on Ruff’s parser. Its HN post says it moved from Python to Rust and can check CPython in under a second.

    Discussion — Users praised its speed and reported true positives, but others found false positives in Django and Flask projects. Discussion focused on the definition of dead code, library versus application analysis, and configuration for framework conventions.

  6. Show HN: Gawain – Require type hints on all Python variables

    • Python
    • Software Development

    67 points · 64 comments · 15 Nov 2026, 04:39 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — Gawain is a Python type-annotation checker that requires annotations on variables, parameters, returns, and class attributes, then invokes ty or pyrefly to check them.

    Discussion — Discussion split between enthusiasm for stricter long-lived Python codebases and criticism that mandatory annotations on every variable duplicate type inference and make Python less pleasant. Readers compared it with existing type checkers and strict languages.

    Week of 2026-11-20

  7. Jonathan Blow – If AI solved coding, why is my software still the same? [video]

    • AI
    • Software Development

    495 points · 752 comments · 13 Nov 2026, 15:08 (Europe/London) · HN discussion

    Story — In a video discussion, Jonathan Blow and Wolf Tivy argued that AI has not yet made software meaningfully better despite its coding capabilities, emphasizing software complexity and the difference between generating code and improving systems.

    Discussion — The thread debated whether AI improves programming today, what counts as better software, and whether complexity stems from technical choices, organizational incentives, or user demands. Readers also discussed the video’s claims about tooling and abstraction.
